chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Mosby's Blue Blowers personnel, 1930-34
summary: Willard lists Mosby's bands, including Lawrence Brown and Marshal Royal; Spikes thinks the 1933-34 touring group was a pickup band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Lawrence Brown and Parker Berry on trombone; Marshal Royal, Leo Davis, alto sax; Johnny Mitchell, tenor sax; Walter Johnson, piano; Ceele Burke, guitar; Ike Perkins, string bass; Baby Lewis, drums... '30-'31 period is what this is of... Mosby's...

And from '33 to '34, "Mosby fronted the band for the show 'Change Your Luck' which went on... an extensive Midwestern tour." He had Leroy Huston, Gene Prince, Theodore "Wingy" Carpenter on trumpet, Baron Willie Moorehead, trombone; William Johnson, Clester Wells, John Mitchell, reeds; Wilbert Barranco, piano; William Dirvin, guitar; Julius Harris, bass, and Red Saunders, drums. Were all those people from Los Angeles?
I don't remember a lot of those people. What year was that? '34?
Maybe some of them came from someplace else. Maybe he recruited the band from...

Yeah. He didn't have none of the... lot of those... were, not the old musicians around town, you see. He hasn't got... he hasn't got Paul. He hasn't got Ashford and the regular ones that he had in his band.
I don't know, it might have been a pick-up band, and he fronted for them.
